source.title: Weak-to-Strong Jailbreaking on Large Language Models
source.authors: Xuandong Zhao; Xianjun Yang; Tianyu Pang; Chao Du; Lei Li; Yu-Xiang Wang; William Yang Wang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes aligned models on 100 adversarial examples and measures harmful-request attack success, directly applying the harmful fine-tuning intervention. It also measures token-distribution differences and tests decoding-time attacks.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's adversarial fine-tuning results, its Figure 1 KL-divergence analysis, and reported attack-success rates for suffix, prefix, decoding-parameter, and weak-to-strong attacks. The cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows. The paper also reports similarity scores, defense results, human-evaluation correlations, and other attack outcomes not included here; these do not directly measure the listed claim versions or are additional settings beyond the 60-row limit.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-trained chat models on 100 harmful examples and reports ASR, the original V1 method. It also reports per-token KL between Llama2 chat models and a harmfully fine-tuned variant over response positions (V3). It measures ASR under decoding-parameter search, a transferred GCG suffix, in-prompt prefix injection and its weak-to-strong logit attack (V4). The V3 comparison uses a jailbroken fine-tuned model, not the base model, so it is a variant method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that safe and jailbroken models differ mainly in early decoding positions, so safety alignment is shallow, and that a weak unsafe model can steer a strong safe model's decoding to >99% ASR. One correction: the gradient-ascent defense reduces ASR by 20–40% for decoding-parameter attacks but only 5–10% for weak-to-strong.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies adversarial fine-tuning on 100 harmful examples, alongside token-distribution analysis and a new weak-to-strong decoding attack. It is not a reproduction of the full original studies' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by target model, dataset, and attack method. The paper states larger amplification factor α increases harmfulness; system-prompt settings are also tested and reported as near-perfect, but their individual rows are not included here.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-10 token overlap between safe and unsafe models rises from about 50% to over 60% with prefix length (Figure 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safe and jailbroken models share most top-ranked tokens, and overlap grows over the response.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient ascent on 200 harmful pairs cuts Llama2-13B ASR by 20–40% for decoding attacks and 5–10% for weak-to-strong (Figure 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful-answer unlearning partially reduces decoding-time jailbreaks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267 (2025)
record.problems: Figure 1 provides no numerical KL values. The KL comparison is between safe and adversarially fine-tuned unsafe models rather than an aligned model and its base model. The reported attack success depends on the tested model, dataset, and attack configuration. The authors note that the attack requires access to logits and that closed-source effectiveness remains unverified.
record.rows_left_out: Not included: Table 5 SALAD-Bench and SORRY-Bench ASRs; Table 7 Chinese and French results; Table 8 system-prompt results; the additional Llama 3 results; and the defense ASR reductions in Figure 5. These are further attack or defense conditions beyond the selected rows. Other metrics such as harmfulness scores, output similarity, and human-evaluation correlations do not measure the listed versions' core outcomes. Figure 2's top-token overlap is related to but distinct from per-token KL.

untested.parts: Only 100 examples are used; there is no sweep from a few to a few hundred examples.
Untested against the base (pretrained) model; only a jailbroken fine-tuned comparator is used. No numeric KL values are given.
Assistant-response prefilling is not run (prefix injection is in the prompt). The suffix is transferred, not optimized on the target.
The authors assert shallowness but do not test whether data or the training objective causes it.
Untested. The gradient-ascent defense is unlearning on harmful answers, not position-spread safety training.

missing.what: Weak-to-Strong† using the unaligned base Llama2-7B as the unsafe guide: ASR 39.8/37.0 (13B) and 35.7/35.0 (70B)
A 1.3B Sheared-LLaMA guide reaches 74.0% ASR against Llama2-70B on AdvBench
Llama2-Unsafe-7B reaches 94.6/94.1 ASR vs Safe-13B at 13.9/12.8 on SALAD-Bench and SORRY-Bench
Weak-to-strong attack with a system prompt still reaches 96.5–100 ASR

record.verdict_notes: Adversarial fine-tuning is used mainly as a tool and baseline, citing Qi et al. and Yang et al., but the paper reports its own ASRs. The V3 evidence is figure-only and uses an unsafe fine-tuned comparator with forced unsafe-token prefixes. Rows r42–r45 duplicate r26–r29. Vicuna and InternLM safe baselines are already high, so those rows are weakly informative.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests adversarial harmful fine-tuning with 100 examples; it does not test a range extending from a few to a few hundred examples.
Ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning is not tested.
The comparisons use an adversarially fine-tuned unsafe model, not a base model; exact KL values are not reported in text.
GCG suffixes, an injected harmful prefix, and decoding-parameter changes are tested. A compliant opening prefilling condition is not separately tested.
No localization of safety to a small set of weights or ranks is tested.
The proposed explanation concerns initial-token distribution differences, but the study does not test whether the data or training objective causes shallowness.
The gradient-ascent defense is not tested as a method for spreading safety across response positions or for maintaining such deepening.
